text:
sam: Hey team — escalated customer issue. Streaming response cuts off after ~70–90s, client reconnects and gets a 401 on the resumed request. Customer is seeing double billing for the same logical session. Repro steps below, logs attached. ✋

jess: Ack. Can you paste topology + sample request ids? Also which LB (ALB/NLB/CF) in front?

sam: Topology: client -> Cloudflare (std) -> ALB (layer7) -> envoy sidecar -> inference svc (go)
Sample request id: req=rc-20260310-77f1

sam: Repro (local/narrow):
```
# using curl to mimic streaming SSE
TOKEN=ey...customer-token
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/stream?prompt=hello&session=123" > /tmp/out.log
```
If I let it run, after ~75s the stream stops mid-chunk (no final event), curl exits with RC 56 sometimes. Then the client immediately reconnects using same token and gets HTTP/1.1 401. Server logs show the original stream was closed by upstream with FIN (no app-side end-of-stream).

liam_edge: Do you have packet-level-ish logs? Any ALB idle timeout events?

sam: Snippet from envoy access / inference logs (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] req=rc-20260310-77f1 upstream=10.1.4.22:8080 status=200 stream=active
[2026-03-10T14:13:18Z] req=rc-20260310-77f1 upstream=10.1.4.22:8080 status=200 stream=partial FIN_BY_PEER
[2026-03-10T14:13:20Z] token=ey... validation=ok reconnect=req=rc-20260310-77f1-reconn status=401 auth=stale_cookie
```
ALB logs show a 60s idle timeout triggered around the same time: target_response_time ~ 75s, elb_status_code = 504 for a handful of attempts.

ana_sre: (jumping in) That pattern looks like ALB idle timeout + proxy buffering/coalescing. If no bytes are flushed for >60s ALB will close. Applications that rely on infrequent partial chunks (small SSE keepalive comments) can have their data coalesced by envoy/nginx or the runtime (golang bufio) and then ALB sees silence.

jess: Confirmed customer app flushes tokens only every 30–90s depending on model. If intermediate chunks are very small (single newline / colon comment), they may be buffered by TCP/Nagle or the proxy.

sam: Repro with python client (sseclient) reproduces reliably with small events. Steps I used: send a single SSE comment every 40s from server, remove heartbeat, run behind ALB -> disconnect.

liam_edge: Quick mitigation options:
- increase ALB idle_timeout to 600s (if customer permits)
- ensure server flushes >1KB every Xs or send a single space/newline repeated to force flush
- disable upstream buffering in envoy/nginx (proxy_buffering off / flush_headers / chunked responses)
- enable TCP keepalive on ALB target group / backend sockets

sam: I tried forcing a 15s comment heartbeat from the app: `print(":heartbeat\n\n", flush=True)` — that prevents disconnect. But customer cannot change model flush frequency easily.

ana_sre: Another wrinkle: after ALB closes the client connection, the customer client retries using the same long-lived bearer token. Our auth service occasionally evicts session state on seeing half-closed streams (we run a short-lived cache for rate limiting), so the token is treated as stale and returns 401. That explains the billing/reconnect loop: client tries again, gets 401, refreshes token, replays request and incurrs another charge.

jess: Ok — actionable plan:
1) Support: advise customer immediate workaround — add a short heartbeat (SSE comment) every 15–20s OR raise ALB idle_timeout to >300s.
2) SRE/Edge: evaluate making edge/proxy flush small chunks immediately and enabling tcp_keepalive on target connections.
3) Product/Auth: investigate why half-closed streams cause token cache eviction; we should not invalidate tokens on upstream FINs without explicit auth error.

liam_edge: I filed infra ticket INF-5923 to run a quick A/B on staging with `proxy_buffering off` and `tcp_keepalive on` for the target group. Will also test Envoy's `buffer_limits` and `flush_on_trailing_headers`.

sam: Repro steps for SRE (copied):
1. Deploy a tiny server that emits: `:hb\n\n` every 40s (SSE comment) and a small data chunk every 90s.
2. Put it behind ALB + Cloudflare as customer runs.
3. Run `curl -N` or python sseclient and watch for FIN after ~60–90s.
4. Observe ALB access log idle_timeout and envoy target logs `FIN_BY_PEER`.

jess: Also collected a short pcap from customer (sanitized) showing the last data frame from server is ~18 bytes, then no wire bytes for 66s, then ALB sends FIN. Sharing a link to sanitized trace: https://internal.redwood/traces/rc-20260310-77f1 (internal)

ana_sre: For the auth side: @product-auth let's not evict tokens on half-close events. I'll open a follow-up with PRD-Auth.

sam: Customer accepted temporary workaround (heartbeat) and asked for ETA. They are on a high-throughput plan so billing duplicates are visible.

jess: Thanks. I'll coordinate with Edge and Auth owners. Tagging @liam_edge and @ana_sre for the infra playbook and @product-auth for token handling changes. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: There is a staged job INF-5923 that will run nightly for 3 runs with `proxy_buffering` toggles. See job 8945.

ana_sre: Next steps for us: run repro in staging today, confirm fix, then propose customer-facing bulletin with recommended config + short-term change (increase ALB idle_timeout or heartbeat).

sam: I'll keep the thread updated with customer confirmation once they apply heartbeat or ALB change. Thanks all.
